title: Bank fraud & card support
description: Card and fraud answers that protect the customer: freeze first, never ask for full credentials.

train.prompt: A customer sees a card payment they do not recognise.
train.completion: Freeze the card in the app now, then check the merchant name with the customer. If it is fraud, cancel the card and open a dispute.

train.prompt: A caller says they are from the bank and asks for my PIN. Is that normal?
train.completion: No. The bank never asks for your PIN or full password. Hang up and call the number on the back of your card.

train.prompt: A customer lost their debit card.
train.completion: Block the card immediately in the app or by phone, check recent transactions, and order a replacement card.

train.prompt: Can I reverse a transfer a customer sent to the wrong account?
train.completion: A completed transfer cannot be reversed directly. Raise a recall request with the receiving bank and explain it is not guaranteed.

train.prompt: A customer was told to move their money to a 'safe account' by the police.
train.completion: This is a known scam. Tell them not to move any money, end the call, and report it to the fraud team.

train.prompt: A customer wants to raise their daily transfer limit for a house deposit.
train.completion: Verify their identity with strong authentication, then raise the limit temporarily for the amount and date they need.

train.prompt: My card was declined abroad but I have money.
train.completion: Check whether the payment was blocked by fraud checks. Confirm the transaction with the customer and unblock the card if it is genuine.

train.prompt: A customer received a text with a link to 'verify their account'.
train.completion: Tell them not to click the link. The bank does not send login links by text. Ask them to forward it to the scam reporting number.

train.prompt: Can I tell a caller the balance of their partner's account?
train.completion: No. Only the account holder or someone with formal authority can get account information.

train.prompt: A customer says an online shop charged them but never sent the item.
train.completion: Ask them to contact the shop first. If it does not resolve it, open a card dispute with the order details and dates.

train.prompt: Someone used my card details online but I still have the card.
train.completion: Freeze the card now, report the transactions as fraud, and order a new card with a new number.

train.prompt: A customer wants to withdraw a large amount of cash urgently for a 'friend in trouble'.
train.completion: Ask calm questions about who asked for the money, because this matches common scams. Involve the fraud team before processing it.

val.prompt: A customer gave their card details to a fake delivery website.
val.completion: Cancel the card now, check for any payments made since, and send a replacement card.

val.prompt: Can you read me the full card number over the phone?
val.completion: No. For security we never read out full card numbers. You can see the details in the app after logging in.

val.prompt: An investment advisor on social media promises 30 percent monthly returns.
val.completion: This is very likely an investment scam. Do not send money, and report the account to the fraud team.

val.prompt: I see a small 1 dollar payment I do not know.
val.completion: Small test payments are often used by fraudsters. Freeze the card and report it before larger payments follow.
